title: Trump’s Helicopter Involved in Air-Traffic Safety Incident
author: Jenna Monnin
summary: The White House said “at no point was the President in harm’s way,” but federal aviation officials are reviewing the incident.
content: Jose Luis Magana/AP Photo/Jose Luis Magana The Federal Aviation Administration is looking into a safety incident involving President Donald Trump’s helicopter and air-traffic control at a nearby airport. When Marine One — the call sign for the aircraft carrying the president — took off from the White House on Tuesday, air-traffic controllers had not halted flights at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport as required by federal aviation standards, The Wall Street Journal first reported. The incident triggered what the FAA calls a loss of standard separation, potentially placing Marine One closer than the acceptable range between aircraft required by federal aviation rules: 1.5 miles horizontally and feet vertically. “Based on our preliminary safety review, there was momentary loss of separation after which the aircraft continued to move away from one another,” the FAA told NOTUS in an emailed statement. “The air traffic controller was in contact with both the commercial pilot and Marine One pilot during the loss of separation.” FAA officials are “continuing to review the incident and will implement any appropriate corrective actions” based on their evaluation. “Marine One flights are piloted by some of the best aviators in the world, and at no point was the President in harm’s way,” White House spokesperson Kush Desai wrote in a statement. Federal aviation officials created new rules for air-traffic control safety after a deadly crash between an American Airlines passenger plane and a military Black Hawk helicopter killed 67 people on Jan. 29, . The two aircraft collided midair and crashed into the Potomac River near Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport. The National Transportation Safety Board found a collection of “systemic failures in airspace design, safety oversight, and risk management” by the FAA and the U.S. Army at fault for the midair collision. The NTSB made 33 safety recommendations to the FAA, which included defining a “close proximity encounter” and maintaining a public database to monitor these events.

title: Helipad Headache
author: Marissa Martinez
content: Aerial view of the work on White House Helipad on August 1, in Washington,D.C. mpi34/mpi34/MediaPunch/IPx Good afternoon. This is the Final NOTUS newsletter for August 4, . You can get it in your inbox every day by signing up here — it’s free! THE LATEST House Ethics opened a probe into Rep. Max Miller (R-Ohio) today after he requested an investigation in hopes of clearing his own name “from these horrific attacks on myself and family.” Sen. Bernie Moreno (R-Ohio), his ex-father-in-law, told reporters today he doesn’t care about the politics of the situation: “This is truly the seventh level of hell. This has been a horrific experience for my entire family.” THE HILL Todd Blanche advanced via committee vote today, but his confirmation is still on thin ice, with several Republicans yet to say they will back the acting attorney general. Sign of the times: “There’s nothing we could do to rein in the president when he said he likes the fund and he wishes it still exists,” Sen. John Cornyn told reporters , reiterating that it’s . “That’s all we could do under these circumstances.” House Republican leadership is privately pushing Rep. Chuck Edwards to drop out after Ethics recommended censuring the North Carolina Republican. The Senate is proposing temporarily blocking a pathway for the White House to cancel grants for any reason at any time. But it wouldn’t undo the administration’s takeover of the federal grants process that’s already underway. THE ADMINISTRATION Trump plans to spend $1.4 billion to keep the National Guard in D.C. until . Trump ordered changes to the new White House South Lawn helipad, after weeks of around-the-clock work, because of the area’s slope, The Washington Post reports . The big white box U.S. Attorney for D.C. Jeanine Pirro wheeled to the White House? A case of evidence to show Trump that shoddy construction had caused the Reflecting Pool damage, CBS reports . THE COURTS An appeals court blocked Trump from rescinding billions in climate funds issued under former President Joe Biden. Absentee voting in Wisconsin discriminates against disabled voters, a judge ruled today, siding with groups who want to force election officials to allow the electronic casting of ballots. title: Trump Orders Contractors to Redo Weeks of Work on White House Helipad
author: Jenna Monnin
summary: Lockheed Martin had agreed to pay for the $5 million project — though it’s unclear if the company intends to cover the additional costs.
content: Workers have already begun dismantling the -foot-wide granite presidential seal placed on top of Trump’s White House helipad. AP Images Contractors are redoing weeks of construction work on President Donald Trump’s White House helipad after he reportedly took issue with its appearance and its slope, which he wants to be more level. The changes, first reported by The Washington Post , are already underway. Photos taken by The Associated Press show contractors removing parts of the -foot-wide presidential seal, made of granite, that had already been installed. The president pushed for the helipad, which is estimated to cost up to $6 million, after a new, more powerful fleet of Marine One helicopters damaged the grass. The project adds to his growing list of renovation projects at the White House and across the nation’s capital. Construction for the helipad began in June, and Trump has reportedly sped up the installation ahead of an “upcoming state visit,” adding $ , to the cost of the project, according to The Washington Post . Documents obtained by the newspaper do not name the foreign leader in question, but officials involved in the construction project requested to expedite the process days after Trump invited Chinese President Xi Jinping to the White House on Sept. 24. “For years, the White House has desperately needed a proper Helipad on White House grounds that will allow the President to land safely and also protect the beautiful South Lawn grass from the fierce exhaust fumes of the incredible Marine One,” White House spokesperson Davis Ingle told NOUTS in a statement Tuesday. It’s unclear if the issues were prompted by safety concerns or aesthetics. In an article about the landscape of the South Lawn, the National Park Service described the incline as a “gradual” slope, and Marine One aircraft have landed on the area for decades without major issue. Federal aviation law does not require helipads to be perfectly level to allow for water runoff. Trump told reporters earlier this month that Lockheed Martin, which owns the helicopter manufacturer Sikorsky, will cover the “about $5 or $6 million” cost of construction because they felt bad about the damage caused by their aircraft. When reached by NOTUS, Lockheed Martin would not say whether it intended to pay for the additional construction. It remains unclear how the construction revision will impact the budget for the project. Clark Construction, the company working on the installation, did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The addition of a White House helipad has been under discussion for years, according to a May report from The Washington Post . Trump has experience planning and building helipads — the Palm Beach Town Council approved the construction of a new helipad at his Mar-a-Lago Club in October, after the president’s first helipad was demolished in at the end of his first term. “The hardest thing to get is a helipad,” Trump said Monday. “There’s no harder zoning thing to get, and I had like seven of them.”

title: Hoosier Hate
author: Marissa Martinez
content: Indiana Senate President Pro Tem Rodric Bray (left) drew President Donald Trump's ire when he helped block a White House-led redistricting push in Indiana last year. Tom Davies/AP Photo Good afternoon. This is the Final NOTUS newsletter for July 31, . You can get it in your inbox every day by signing up here — it’s free! THE LATEST Donald Trump bashed Iran during a Cabinet meeting at Camp David today, calling the country “dishonorable.” But he also blamed a cyberattack on dozens of Minnesota community water systems on Democratic Gov. Tim Walz — not Iran, as U.S. officials suspect . The “anti-weaponization” fund is still alive, Trump suggested in a Truth Social post today. The president lamented that “perhaps there has never been a group of people treated so badly in our nation’s history” as the Jan. 6 rioters, and he reaffirmed they should be “paid back.” Sen. Thom Tillis (R-North Carolina) said Trump’s post “is exactly why we are attempting to formally end” the fund. He and Sen. John Cornyn (R-Texas) are still working with Todd Blanche : “It’s a shame his confirmation has hit a snag only because an incompetent personal advisor to the President refuses to amend the bogus settlement.” THE ADMINISTRATION The Trump administration plans to cut Arizona, California and Nevada’s water usage as Colorado River levels drop to historic lows. Carlos Cordeiro, senior adviser to both Gianni Infantino and the White House World Cup task force, resigned in protest of the FIFA president’s plan to partially privatize the marquee international tournament. The former Goldman Sachs executive said he had no involvement in the proposal and that FIFA’s “responsibility is not to maximise commercial returns at any cost.” Markwayne Mullin’s attempt to cancel the July 4 National Mall celebration over weather concerns in D.C. at the time infuriated Trump, The Free Press reports . THE HILL Rep. Jamie Raskin (D-Maryland), the Judiciary Committee’s top Democrat, announced a new probe into Trump Media’s plan to start charging for early access to the president’s Truth Social posts, which is set to launch tomorrow. Former Rep. George Santos settled a case with the Commodity Futures Trading Commission today after he bet on his own attendance to Trump’s State of the Union address earlier this year. He’ll have to pay a $17, fine and repay the $17, .98 he made on the bet, the CFTC announced. He also is barred from trading on prediction markets for three years. THE STATES Rodric Bray, thea top Republican state senator in Indiana, said he would not seek reelection as the chamber’s president pro tempore after Trump threatened to primary anyone who supported his bid. He will keep his position as a rank-and-file member of the state Senate. Bray incurred the president’s wrath last year when he helped block a White House-led redistricting push in the state. “Better yet would be if he would resign from Office, completely,” Trump said in a good-riddance post on Truth Social. New York Attorney General Letitia James sued Kalshi in state court, alleging the company runs an “illegal gambling operation” without proper licenses.
